questions.question: Is MFA required for every person with access to systems that hold member data, including third-party contractors?
questions.answer: Yes. Every workforce account, employees and contractors alike, signs in through Okta with MFA enforced (Okta Verify push or WebAuthn). This includes the six third-party contractor accounts, which have read-only access to production AWS and access to GitHub. Contractor accounts were moved onto the MFA policy on 2026-11-07; before that date they signed in with a password only, under a temporary onboarding rule.

questions.question: Describe encryption at rest for member data, including key ownership.
questions.answer: Member data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. The production PostgreSQL database (Amazon RDS) and the S3 buckets holding statement files and reconciliation exports are encrypted with a single AWS KMS customer-managed key (alias/ledgerline-data). Ledgerline owns and manages this key in its own AWS account; the key material is held in AWS KMS, rotates automatically every year, and is not supplied or held by customers. The same key protects all customers' data. Reconciliation export files created before 2026-11-07 remain encrypted with AES-256 under S3-managed keys until they expire, no later than 2026-12-07.

Retention was 7 days from March 2026 until 2026-11-07, so the full 14-day history is available from 2026-11-14. Our backup policy sets 35 days, and we plan to restore 35-day retention at our December 2026 review.

questions.question: What is the retention period for security and audit logs?
questions.answer: AWS CloudTrail audit logs (all regions, with log file validation) are retained for 90 days in CloudWatch Logs and for 180 days in an S3 archive encrypted with our AWS KMS key. Application API logs are retained for 30 days. We are extending S3 retention of audit logs to 400 days by 2026-12-31.

questions.question: Is member data shared with any AI model provider?
questions.answer: Yes. Since our August 2026 release, the reconciliation service uses Anthropic's API (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to draft short exception memos for statement lines that cannot be matched to a ledger entry. For each unmatched line we send the counterparty name, amount, value date and remittance text as they appear on the statement, together with the nearest candidate ledger entries. Under our order form with Anthropic, these inputs are deleted within 30 days and are not used to train models. This use did not go through our vendor security review before launch. The DPA with Anthropic is not yet signed; it is due to be signed by 2026-11-21.
